items.summary: The guard's behaviour is settled. The plan's line reference is wrong: the guard is at 160 inside the function, not at 305-309. Reading the code also shows a risk the guard does not cover: a settings-only edit to a shared shot can prefix clip ids a second time. That is a code-read conclusion; nothing was executed and no test covers it.
evidence: App head shotCompositionEditor.ts:157-171 remapIndependentInternalTimeline. :160 guard: if (!timeline || !Array.isArray(timeline.clips)) return internal (clone returned unprefixed). :161-169 prefix each clip with a string id as `${prefix}:${id}`. Only clip ids are touched.

Plan's ':305-309' is not a guard inside the function. Line 305 is the conditional spread of internal_timeline_revision in updateCanonicalShotRevision. The call-site guard is :317 (if (updatedRevision.internal_timeline_revision)) inside if (sharedSource) at :310; the post-remap digest guard is :331. The plan's 148-160 is now 157-171.

Only caller: updateCanonicalShotRevision :318, reached only when sharedSource (:258-261). Settings path: updateCanonicalShotSettings :404-410 -> ShotEditorView.tsx:161 passes no timeline, so updatedInternal is undefined and the stored source clips go through remap again.
Timeline path: updateCanonicalShotTimeline (:476-491) -> shotTimelineDataProvider.ts:1376. On a shared source the output clip ids are prefixed (:169).

Double-prefix path (code read): occ-1 timeline edit on a shared shot gives new shot S1 with ids S1:x (:169). duplicateLinkedOccurrence :628-640 keeps shot_id (withOccurrenceIdentity :103), so occ-3 shares S1. A settings edit on occ-1 then has sharedSource true and remaps S1:x to S2:S1:x. The guard at :160 does not detect already-prefixed ids.

items.item: Whether element frames are clip-local in the renderer
items.summary: Element frames are Remotion Sequence-local, so they are clip-local for an element with no transition, in both App preview and export. With transitions the answer depends on the renderer and the transition policy. Reading settles the mechanism, not the final frame values, which needs a render (not run).
evidence: Remotion (app node_modules, dist/cjs/use-current-frame.js contextOffset): useCurrentFrame() = timeline frame minus (cumulatedFrom + relativeFrom) of the nearest Sequence. Inside a Sequence the frame is Sequence-local.

am-sprite component.tsx:149 useCurrentFrame(); keyframes compared with that frame at :64-66 (key.frame <= sf). am-footage component.tsx:186 same pattern. No component under astrid/packs reads globalFrame.

App preview, effect elements: TimelineRenderer.tsx:1355-1368 -> AstridEffectPreviewSequence (:356-403) mounts Component in <Sequence from=round(clip.at*fps)> (:382-384). Frame 0 = clip start. Transitions ignored on this path.

App preview, animation elements: AstridAnimationPreviewSequence (:405-430) from = secondsToFrames(clip.at) minus transitionFrames when there is a predecessor transition (:417-420, :426). Frame 0 = clip start minus pre-roll.

Export (composition repo): TimelineComposition.tsx:84-112 mounts element EffectComponent inside ClipLook; :166-170 visual clip in <Sequence from={plan.drawStart}>, with TransitionLayer when needsLayer.
No transition: drawStart = span.start (transition-spans.ts:103-104), so clip-local.

Default outgoing dissolve/dip: incoming drawStart moves back by T (transition-spans.ts:139-140); TransitionLayer.tsx:17-19 wraps content in <Freeze frame={contentFrame}>; contentFrame = ownFrame (evaluation.ts:63-64; ownFrame transition-spans.ts:183-190), so the content clock is clip-local. Freeze's frame offset read in freeze.js:43-53 (first part only).

Opt-in preroll-crossfade (only fade/cross-fade may declare it, transitions.tsx:62): no Freeze (TransitionLayer.tsx:17); contentFrame = draw-local (evaluation.ts:64; comment TransitionLayer.tsx:4-6 'keeps this draw-local clock, including preroll'). Element frame 0 is T frames before the clip start. transition-spans.ts:94-97 and :144-145 set the policy.
unverified: Whether the film or the chapters timelines have transitions on am-sprite or other element clips (not checked; the plan does not say).

Final frame values with transitions in App preview vs export. That disagreement (App effects ignore transitions; App animations and export preroll shift frames) needs a 2-clip render, which this brief does not allow.
Freeze's exact frame semantics in the installed Remotion version (read only the first part of freeze.js).
